newsitem.title: USA: Sprint appeals ruling on rehiring workers.
newsitem.headline: Sprint appeals ruling on rehiring workers.

text.p: Sprint Corp has appealed in federal court a ruling by a labor board that ordered it to rehire more than 170 telemarketing workers, a company spokesman said Monday.

Bill White, assistant vice president of corporate communications at the company, told Reuters that Sprint had appealed the ruling by the National Labor Relations Board earlier in the day in federal court in Washington.
"We find it surprising that it (the board) did not uphold the earlier decisions," he said, referring to two previous rulings on the case that favored Sprint.

The board has ordered the company to rehire and pay full back wage and benefit compensation to 177 workers whose telemarketing office was closed in San Francisco in 1994, according to a statement released by the Communications Workers of America on Monday.

The statement said the board found that Sprint's closing of the marketing office, just one week before a scheduled union election, was a violation of federal labor law. The office, called La Conexion Familiar, or Family Connection in Spanish, employed mostly Latin women.

White said the board's ruling overturned two previous decisions on the case, which found the company's reasons for closing to office to be legitimate -- financial losses and a dwindling customer base.

The Communications Workers of America is a union that represents more than 600,000 workers in telecommunications, broadcasting and cable television, journalism and publishing and the public service sector. Sprint employs a total of about 49,000 people throughout the country.
